message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide (and a ready‑to‑copy code snippet) showing **how you would query VirusTotal’s “Domain” endpoint** to fetch all available information about `twitter.com`.  
(Replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with your real key – e.g., `twt_key_abc`.)

---

### 1️⃣ What you’ll hit

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/<DOMAIN>
```

For Twitter:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com
```

> ⚠️ *VirusTotal uses bearer tokens.*  
> Your header must contain:
> ```
> Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>
> ```

---

### 2️⃣ Sample cURL command

```bash
curl -X GET \
     --url "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com" \
     -H "accept: application/json" \
     -H "x-apikey: twt_key_abc"
```

*If you’re using the newer V3 API, replace `x-apikey` with `Authorization: Bearer …`.*

---

### 3️⃣ Quick Python example (`requests`)

```python
import requests

api_key   = "twt_key_abc"          # <-- put your key here
headers   = {"Accept": "application/json",
             "x-apikey": api_key}
endpoint  = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com"

resp      = requests.get(endpoint, headers=headers)
data      = resp.json()

print("Status:", resp.status_code)
if resp.ok:
    print("\n--- Domain Report ---")
    print(f"Name: {data['data']['id']}")
    print(f"Last Analysis Stats:")
    for engine, count in data['data'].get('attributes', {}).get(
            'last_analysis_stats', {}).items():
        print(f"  {engine}: {count}")

else:
    print("Error fetching domain info.")
```

> 📌 If you prefer the older V2 API, just change the URL to `/v2/domain/report`.

---

### 4️⃣ Typical JSON payload structure (V3)

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `data.id` | Domain name (`twitter.com`) |
| `data.attributes.last_analysis_date` | Unix timestamp of most recent scan |
| `data.attributes.last_analysis_results` | Per‑scanner verdicts |
| `data.attributes.last_analysis_stats` | Aggregated counts per result type (`harmless`, `malicious`, `undetected`, etc.) |
| `data.relationships.submissions.data[*].id` | List of submission IDs linked to the domain |

*(See [VT docs](https://developers.virustotal.com/reference/get-domain-report-v3) for full schema)*

---

### 5️⃣ Things to keep in mind

| ✅ Tip | Why it matters |
|--------|----------------|
| **Rate Limits** | Free tier → ~4 req/min; paid tiers higher. Exceeding will return HTTP 429. |
| **Pagination** | For domains with many submissions, results may span multiple pages—use `next_page_token`. |
| **Caching** | Repeated queries for the same domain within short intervals might hit cache; consider storing locally. |
| **Privacy & Terms** | Only request public data; respect VT’s terms of service. |

---

#### TL;DR

Just send a simple authenticated GET request to  

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/twitter.com
```

with your API key in the header, parse the returned JSON, and you have everything VT has recorded about that domain—including malware detections, reputation scores, associated URLs, IP addresses, and more. Happy scanning!
